$comment: China counterfactual: the NPC adopts a comprehensive AI Law that hardens the soft-law frontier framework into statute and codifies tiered high-risk duties. Filing and labeling are already statute-grade and are left unchanged.

frontier.basis: Frontier safety duties become mandatory under statute.

highrisk.basis: Tiered risk classification widens and deepens use-specific duties.

filing.basis: The defining feature: public-facing generative AI must pass CAC filing (security self-assessment, test-question banks, keyword filtering, refusal-rate checks) before launch. 1,112 services filed and 731 apps/features registered by 2026-08-31; batches every ~2 months.

content.basis: Mandatory explicit + implicit labeling of AI-generated content (Labeling Measures and GB 45438-2025, both from 2025-09-01), deep-synthesis provisions, and content controls aligned to core socialist values. The highest-cost slot because content moderation is continuous, not one-off.

data.basis: PIPL, Data Security Law, Network Data Security Management Regulations (2025), the relaxed 2024 cross-border data-flow rules, and the Cybersecurity Law amendment effective 2026-01-01 that adds AI provisions.

trade.basis: China's own outbound controls as borne by Chinese AI firms selling abroad: the technology-export catalogue (covers recommendation algorithms) and dual-use/rare-earth regimes. Inbound chip restrictions are modelled in compute, not here.

fragmentation.basis: Regulation is centralised in CAC with MIIT/MOST/SAMR co-signers; local AI promotion regulations (Shanghai, Shenzhen) add light layers. Few regimes, each heavy.

reference_firm.basis: Same reference firm as the US binding, so fixed_burden is comparable.

ex_ante_gate.basis: CAC filing typically takes several months from submission to listing; 4 is a central estimate. Same obsolescence as the US binding.

state_support.basis: Compute vouchers, local-government AI funds, the national AI industry investment fund (2025), and the AI+ action plan's procurement pull. Larger than the US offset, which is what lets net_burden understate the filing regime's friction.

compute.basis: Domestic accelerators (Ascend, Cambricon, Hygon, Kunlunxin, Moore Threads, MetaX) cover ~55% of demand. The January 2026 BIS rule licenses H200-class imports case-by-case (~25% of demand), but Beijing has blocked H200s at customs and steered buyers domestic, so ~15% of licensed volume lands. Grey channels (transshipment, offshore cloud) add ~8%.
